subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Roasting: Where Margins Live
description: A quick win: understand Roasting: Where Margins Live.

hook.text: Green coffee beans cost $2–5 per pound. Roast them and the price jumps to $10–20. That's where margin lives.

buildup.text: Roasting is the most profitable step in the chain. It transforms a commodity into a branded consumer product.

discovery.text: Large roasters like Nestlé and JDE Peet's control over 40% of global roasted coffee sales combined.

twist.text: Almost all roasting happens in consuming countries—Europe, the US, Japan. Producing countries roast less than 10%.

climax.text: If origin countries roasted and branded their own coffee, billions in value would shift from North to South.

punchline.text: Roasting is just heat. But it captures most of the profit.

quiz.question: Where does most coffee roasting happen?
options: In consuming countries like Europe and the US

details.summary: Roasting is where the highest margins in the coffee chain are captured. Green coffee is a low-margin commodity, but roasted coffee sells at many times the raw price. The transformation from green beans to roasted product is where most of coffee's retail value is created.
details.whyItMatters: The roasting step captures disproportionate value in the supply chain. This is why producing countries increasingly want to roast and export finished product.
takeaways: Roasting captures the highest margins in the coffee chain
Green coffee trades for a fraction of the roasted price
Producing countries want to capture roasting value locally

faq.question: Why do most producing countries export green beans?
faq.answer: Historical trade structures and import tariffs favor raw commodity exports. Consuming countries impose lower tariffs on green coffee than roasted. Roasting also requires proximity to consumers for freshness. These factors keep most roasting in consuming countries like the US and Europe.

faq.question: How much does roasting increase coffee's value?
faq.answer: Green coffee might trade at 3 to 5 dollars per pound, while roasted specialty coffee sells for 15 to 25 dollars per pound retail. The roasting process itself costs a few dollars per pound in energy and labor, meaning most of the markup is margin and brand value.
